messages:
Alex (support): heads-up, customer (Acme) reports embeddings shape mismatch across deployments. Hosted -> 1024, Dedicated -> 768, Private -> 1024. They rely on 1024 vectors in downstream index. Can eng take a look?

Priya (eng-runtime): on it. can you paste the raw request and response shapes they saw? ideally minimal repro.

Alex (support): pasted from customer logs below. note they call the same endpoint + model alias in each env.
```
# curl they used (sanitized)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed/clip-alias","input":["cat","dog","car"]}'
```
Customer parsed shapes after converting JSON arrays -> numpy arrays:
- Hosted: response.embeddings shape = (3, 1024)
- Dedicated: response.embeddings shape = (3, 768)
- Private: response.embeddings shape = (3, 1024)

Alex (support): they also attached raw first vector (truncated) lengths: Hosted len(vec[0])=1024, Dedicated len(vec[0])=768. No error returned, just different length. Billing unaffected but app fails when indexing.

Priya (eng-runtime): thanks. first suspicion: model alias "embed/clip-alias" might map to different underlying checkpoints in Dedicated. dims change only if model variant is different (different head size), not quantization. can we get model metadata from each control plane?

Eli (eng-platform): I queried the model registry for the alias on each env:
```
# hosted
GET https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models/embed%2Fclip-alias/metadata
=> {"id":"embed/clip-v2","output_dimension":1024,"revision":"v2.1"}
# dedicated control plane (dedicated-pool-a)
GET https://dedicated.dcp.redwood.internal/v1/models/embed%2Fclip-alias/metadata
=> {"id":"embed/clip-compact","output_dimension":768,"revision":"v1.9"}
# private (customer VPC)
GET https://private.acme.local/models/embed%2Fclip-alias/metadata
=> {"id":"embed/clip-v2","output_dimension":1024,"revision":"v2.1"}
```
Eli (eng-platform): so alias resolved to different concrete model (embed/clip-compact) in Dedicated. that explains dim change. looks like a bad alias sync during the dedicated rollout.

Maya (sre): when did the dedicated pool last get a model sync? deploy logs show an alias sync job at 2026-01-22T03:12:10Z failed and later retried. deploy-bot gave a green for runtime but model registry sync error slipped by.

deploy-bot: "model-sync-job(dedicated-pool-a) failed: checksum mismatch for alias mapping; retry scheduled"

Priya (eng-runtime): thanks. immediate remediation: we should pin alias on dedicated to the correct model id (embed/clip-v2) and restart the model router on the pool so cached mappings clear. steps I recommend:
1) run admin alias update on dedicated control plane: POST /admin/aliases {alias: "embed/clip-alias", model_id: "embed/clip-v2"} 
2) trigger model-router restart for pool dedicated-pool-a (rolling)
3) run sanity check: call embeddings on dedicated with wording below and assert shape==1024 for batch sizes 1..8

Alex (support): can you paste the sanity check script snippet we can run and give to customer if they want to self-validate?

Priya (eng-runtime): pasted quick python repro they can run locally against any env: 
```python
import requests
import numpy as np

def call(url, key):
  r = requests.post(url, headers={"Authorization":f"Bearer {key}"}, json={"model":"embed/clip-alias","input":["a","b","c"]})
  r.raise_for_status()
  embs = r.json()["data"]  # list of lists
  shapes = [len(x) for x in embs]
  print(url, shapes)

# run against hosted/dedicated/private endpoints
```

Priya (eng-runtime): also added a server-side quick guard: if metadata.output_dimension != len(embeddings[0]) log a high-priority alert and return HTTP 500 with message "model-output-dimension-mismatch". pushing that as hotfix to runtime for a few hours to catch any other drift.

Eli (eng-platform): I updated the dedicated alias mapping at 2026-03-01T14:43:12Z and kicked a model-router rolling restart for dedicated-pool-a.

deploy-bot: "alias-update(embed/clip-alias -> embed/clip-v2) applied to dedicated-pool-a by Eli; model-router restart queued"

Maya (sre): after restart we ran the parity suite (batch sizes 1,2,4,8; random seed fixed) across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. results: all returned output_dimension=1024 and cosine similarity between Hosted/Dedicated medians > 0.995.

Jason (customer-ops): customer verified on their side after 30m and reported their indexing job moved forward. they asked what caused it and whether this could happen again.

Eli (eng-platform): root cause summary for CS: alias mapping drift during dedicated pool sync due to a checksum mismatch bug in alias-sync job; caused dedicated to resolve alias to an older smaller model. not a model server bug. fix applied and we've patched sync job to retry with backoff and alert on checksum disagreement.

Alex (support): great. can we add two follow-ups for internal tasks?
- add a nightly parity check comparing model metadata and a single sample embedding dim across Hosted/Dedicated/Private for all public aliases.
- add a proactive alert when alias mapping changes to a model with different output_dimension than previous mapping.

Priya (eng-runtime): filed infra ticket INF-8123 with those tasks, assigned to platform eng.

Maya (sre): marking incident "resolved" for the embedding-dim drift, and documenting mitigation steps in runbook.

Alex (support): closing loop with customer and sent a short explain email + postmortem. :white_check_mark:

Jason (customer-ops): customer appreciated the quick turnaround. left a :thumbsup: reaction on the support thread.

Priya (eng-runtime): notes for future troubleshooting (internal):
- always compare model metadata.output_dimension across envs first.
- if dims differ, check alias->model_id mapping, not batching. batching issues usually show up as shape mismatch within a response (e.g., ragged arrays) or errors, not reduced dims.
- add a small CI job that hits every alias with batch sizes 1..4 and asserts consistent dim.

Alex (support): thanks all. documenting thread in the customer ticket and linking to INF-8123.
